notes: Offline eval. The skill posts inline comments to a real pull request, so these test DECISION and PROCESS behaviour rather than live posting: request resolution, the REVIEW.md gate, verification labelling, and how many findings post. Run each with no network and with posting disabled, and tell the runner to record what it WOULD post rather than posting it. A run that stops at a question it must ask the user is a complete and valid outcome. Fixtures are described in fixture_setup rather than committed, because two of them are git repositories and one needs an unreadable file, neither of which travels well in version control. Assertions carry passed=null until a run fills them in.

evals.name: no-pr-given
evals.fixture_setup: mkdir repo && cd repo && git init && git remote add origin https://github.com/acme/widgets.git && commit a cart.js with an off-by-one loop on main, then `git checkout -b feat/cart-total` and commit one more change. No pull request exists.
evals.expected_output: The skill has no pull request. It asks which pull request to review and stops. It does not review the checked-out feature branch, does not run a diff against the base branch, and does not offer a choice between reviewing a PR and reviewing the local branch.

assertions.text: Asks which pull request to review
Does not review the checked-out branch
Does not offer a local-branch review option
Stops without posting anything

evals.name: url-beats-remote
evals.fixture_setup: Same fixture as eval 0. The point is that the working directory's origin remote is github.com while the request URL given in the prompt is gitlab.com.
evals.prompt: can you review https://gitlab.com/acme/widgets/-/merge_requests/42 for me. no network available so just tell me exactly how you'd resolve the forge, the repository, the request number and which CLI you'd use, then stop before running anything.
evals.expected_output: Resolves GitLab from the URL rather than from the GitHub origin remote. Takes owner=acme, repo=widgets, number=42 from the URL itself. Names glab as the CLI. Refers to it as a merge request and an MR number, never a pull request. Does not use the working directory's github.com remote to decide the forge.

assertions.text: Identifies GitLab from the URL
Does not let the github.com remote decide the forge
Extracts owner=acme, repo=widgets, number=42 from the URL
Names glab as the CLI
Uses merge request vocabulary
Carries `--repo acme/widgets` on every subsequent call rather than re-resolving from the working directory

evals.name: volume-control-on-rereview
evals.fixture_setup: No repository needed. The prompt supplies the completed analysis output inline or as an attached file: 1 Important, 1 Pre-existing, 9 Nits, one open human thread, zero open skill threads, and one RESOLVED thread whose first comment contains `code-review`.
evals.prompt: The analysis is already done, results attached. Apply the posting rules and tell me exactly which findings get posted and what the summary section says. Do not post anything; just tell me.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this is a re-review because the Any-skill-thread set is non-empty (a resolved skill thread counts). Posts the 1 Important and the 1 Pre-existing. Posts ZERO of the 9 nits, because on a re-review no new nit is posted at all, not merely 5 of them. Summary reports the nits held back and does not claim a clean review.

assertions.text: Recognises this as a re-review
Counts a resolved skill thread as evidence of a prior review
Posts zero new nits
Posts the Important and the Pre-existing finding
Summary reports the nits held back
Does not present the review as clean
Resolves no thread, because the open skill thread set is empty, and leaves the human thread at cart.js:12 alone
The severity table counts posted findings, so the Nit row reads 0 rather than 9

evals.name: verification-drops-uncited-claim
evals.fixture_setup: No repository needed. The prompt supplies five candidates C1-C5 and states, for each, what evidence it holds. C1 is a behaviour claim about a second file with no citation; C4 is a Removed-behaviour claim citing the current file rather than a removal in the diff.
evals.prompt: Here are the raw candidates from the angles. Run the verification step on them and tell me, for each one, the label you assign and whether it posts.
evals.expected_output: C1 is DROPPED entirely: it is a behaviour claim with no citation, so it never posts and never reaches the summary counts, and it is not downgraded to a lower severity or to plausible. C2 is CONFIRMED and posts. C3 is PLAUSIBLE and posts, labelled as such. C4 is dropped or rejected because a Removed-behaviour finding must cite the removal in the diff and the diff shows no removal. C5 posts as a Nit with the diff as its evidence, since the citation rule applies to behaviour claims only.

assertions.text: C1 is dropped entirely
C1 is not merely downgraded
C2 is CONFIRMED and posts, because its cited line settles the off-by-one
C3 is PLAUSIBLE and posts
C4 is rejected for citing the file rather than the removal
C5 posts with the diff as its evidence
The PLAUSIBLE-by-default list is applied conditionally, not by defect shape alone

evals.name: unreadable-review-md-stops
evals.fixture_setup: Same fixture as eval 0, plus a REVIEW.md at the repository root that cannot be read as a file (create it as a directory: `mkdir REVIEW.md`).
evals.prompt: review PR 7 on this repo please
evals.expected_output: Finds REVIEW.md at the repository root, fails to read it as a file, and stops the review naming the file and the error. Posts nothing and leaves the pull request untouched. Does not silently continue as though no REVIEW.md existed.

assertions.text: Attempts to read REVIEW.md at the repository root
Detects that REVIEW.md cannot be read as a file
Stops the review
Names the file and the error
Posts nothing and leaves the request untouched
Does not treat the unreadable file as an absent one
Does not repair REVIEW.md itself: it may show the commands but must not run them
Prints no Reviewer To-Do section, because the issue and test plan check never ran

evals.name: reports-helpfulness-feedback
evals.fixture_setup: No repository needed. The prompt supplies completed analysis output plus thread state in which three earlier skill comments carry reactions: two THUMBS_UP and one THUMBS_DOWN across three threads, one of them resolved.
evals.prompt: Analysis is done, results attached, and I've reacted to some of your earlier comments. Apply the posting rules and tell me exactly what you'd post and what the summary says. Don't post anything.
evals.expected_output: Recognises a re-review, so posts the Important finding and no new nits. Reports the helpfulness verdicts on the Feedback line: 2 of 3 marked helpful, 1 not helpful, counting the resolved thread's reaction. Does not act on the single thumbs down beyond reporting it: nothing is suppressed, no pattern is silenced, and the finding at that line is not dropped for having been disliked.

assertions.text: Reports a Feedback line with the helpfulness counts
Counts the resolved thread's reaction, not only the open ones
Does not suppress or silence anything on the strength of one thumbs down
Still applies the re-review rule: posts the Important finding and zero new nits
Does not write to the agent-pattern registry

evals.name: declaration-answers-scenario
evals.fixture_setup: No repository needed. The prompt supplies the request's commit bodies, its body, its linked issue, and its diff inline. The issue carries three acceptance criteria. One commit body holds a coverage declaration that records criteria 1 and 2 as covered and criterion 3 as manual, with the reason that the repository has no rendering runner. The request body names criterion 3 under Manual verification. The diff adds tests for criteria 1 and 2 only.
evals.prompt: Here is the pull request, its commit bodies, its linked issue, and its diff. Run the issue and test plan check on it. Tell me every finding you would file, every Reviewer To-Do bullet you would print, and what the summary would carry.
evals.expected_output: The check reads the declaration out of the commit bodies the prompt supplied, rather than asking for a checkout. Criterion 3 files no missing-test finding and gets no Reviewer To-Do bullet, because the declaration records it as manual and the request body names it under Manual verification. The summary carries a Declared manual line counting one scenario. Criteria 1 and 2 raise nothing, because the diff tests both.

assertions.text: Reads the declaration from the request's commit bodies, not from a checked-out branch
Files no missing-test finding for criterion 3
Adds no Reviewer To-Do bullet for criterion 3
The summary carries a Declared manual line counting 1 scenario
Criteria 1 and 2 raise nothing from this check

evals.name: no-declaration-keeps-todo
evals.fixture_setup: No repository needed. The prompt supplies the request's commit bodies, its body, its linked issue, and its diff inline. No commit body carries a declaration, because no harness skill produced this branch. The issue carries three acceptance criteria and the diff adds tests for two of them.
evals.prompt: Here is the pull request, its commit bodies, its linked issue, and its diff. Run the issue and test plan check on it. Tell me every finding you would file, every Reviewer To-Do bullet you would print, and what the summary would carry.
evals.expected_output: The check finds no declaration, records that, and continues. The untested criterion files a red Important finding and gets a Reviewer To-Do bullet, exactly as it did before the declaration step existed. The absence of a declaration is not reported as a finding, and no Declared manual line prints, because its count is zero.

assertions.text: Records that the branch carries no declaration and continues
Files a red Important finding for the untested criterion
Adds a Reviewer To-Do bullet for the same criterion
Files no finding about the missing declaration
Prints no Declared manual line, because the count is zero

evals.name: cap-runs-before-verification
evals.fixture_setup: No repository needed. The prompt supplies the raw candidate list the angles returned: 40 nit candidates across six angles and 4 Important candidates, of which 12 nits cite a `file:line` and the rest cite nothing. The request carries no review thread at all, and its repository has no `review/agent-patterns.md`.
evals.prompt: Here are the raw candidates from the angles for PR 12, which carries no existing review thread. Walk the analysis from the dedup step onward and tell me, in order, which candidates you verify, which you hold back, and what the summary's Held back line says. Verify nothing you would not post, and post nothing.
evals.expected_output: Step 4 decides how many findings can post before the verification pass runs, so the run verifies 9 candidates rather than 44: the 4 Important candidates, which the cap never counts, and the 5 nits the ranking keeps. The ranking puts a nit that cites a `file:line` ahead of one that cites nothing, then diff order, because no candidate carries a CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE label yet. The Held back line reports the other 35 nits. Nothing is posted.

assertions.text: Applies the nit cap before the verification pass, not after it
Verifies all 4 Important candidates
Verifies 5 nits rather than 40
Ranks a nit that cites a `file:line` above one that cites nothing, rather than ranking on a label it does not have yet
The Held back line reports 35 nits
Caps no Important candidate
Posts nothing, because the prompt disabled posting

evals.name: manifest-check-gated-by-the-suggestion
evals.fixture_setup: No repository needed. The prompt supplies three findings the cap kept, each with its suggestion. F1's suggestion renames a variable in the file's own idiom. F2's suggestion calls `lodash.groupBy`. F3's suggestion runs a `jq` command. The prompt states that the repository has a `package.json` and that it pins lodash at 4.17.20.
evals.prompt: Here are three findings the cap kept, with their suggestions. Run the verification pass on each and tell me which parts of it you ran for each finding, and why.
evals.expected_output: F1 skips the manifest check, because its suggestion names no library, no library API, and no shell command, and its body posts as it stands. F2 runs the check against `package.json` and settles `lodash.groupBy` against the pinned 4.17.20. F3 runs the check because its suggestion carries a shell command. Each finding is handled in one pass, rather than one walk of the list per part.

assertions.text: F1 skips the manifest check
F1's body is unchanged by the skipped check
F2 runs the check against `package.json` and names the pinned version
F3 runs the check because its suggestion carries a shell command
Labels, checks, and classifies each finding in one pass rather than three walks of the list
